hints: Equate $kx^2 - 3x = x - k$ to form $kx^2 - 4x + k = 0$.
Use the condition for no intersection: $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac < 0$.
walkthrough:
Equate the curve and line equations to form a quadratic equation in $x$:
$$kx^2 - 3x = x - k \implies kx^2 - 4x + k = 0$$

Apply the condition for no real intersection, setting the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac < 0$:
$$(-4)^2 - 4(k)(k) < 0 \implies 16 - 4k^2 < 0$$

Solve the inequality for $k$:
$$4k^2 > 16 \implies k^2 > 4 \implies k < -2 \quad\text{or}\quad k > 2$$
